title: Generalize "find a potential indicated element" for shadow roots
body:
In <https://w3c.github.io/csswg-drafts/css-values/#local-urls> I'm defining that fragment-only CSS url references (like `url(#foo)`) are always interpreted as ID refs for the current tree, rather than just treating them like a normal URL and looking for the target element. (This is required for SVG references to resolve when used in shadow DOM, for example.)

Right now I'm manually specifying the search algo:

> resolve to the first element
> in [=tree order=]
> among the associated [=node tree=]'s descendants
> with the URL's [=url/fragment=] as its ID.

However, @annevk pointed out the HTML has the ["find a potential indicated element" algo](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#find-a-potential-indicated-element) already, which does basically the same thing.

I'd like to use it, just to cut down on duplication, but currently (a) the algo is defined to specifically take a Document, not a ShadowRoot (or other DocumentFragments), and (b) the algo also searches for `<a name>` matches. I don't really have an opinion on (b) (I'm not reproducing it manually, but could take it or leave it if it was included in the algo by default), but (a) is both currently killer to my usage, and absolutely trivial to fix.

So, at minimum, could we rephrase the algorithm so that it takes a Document or DocumentFragment? This involves swapping out the "in the document tree" references to just be "in the tree".

Additional possible things to do:
* Make the `<a name>` search optional? (Again, I don't really care either way.)
* The higher "indicated part" algorithm for HTML documents tries to "find a potential indicated element" twice, once with the literal fragment and once after percent-decoding and UTF-8 decoding. Should this be built into "find a potential indicated element"? Or is it just a legacy thing that I shouldn't reproduce elsewhere?
